summary: Clean on gore and length, and the batch handles its non-vehicles with real care: the hearse is gentle throughout, the cash machine's 'Out of Order Rest' and 'Card Swallowed' are excellent, the yo-yo, plough Roman coins, dolly 'one very surprised grandad', stroller 'Foldfail', tow truck 'arrives just after you've started it yourself', street sweeper tortoise and electric car Common are strong. Mechanics are mostly respected and kit moves are cleverly re-skinned for prams, signs and trolleys. The same three structural problems as w05 are stronger here. (1) 39 of 79 Legendaries are 'has done X for N years / generations' (58 start with 'Has'), ending on 'still has its original...' or 'never once...' (funicular, model train, monorail, toy train, train, gondola lift, tram, boat trailer, logging truck, truck, cash machine, prams, coupe, hatchback, manhole, parking meter, placard, road sign, scoreboard, sign board, stop sign, street lamp, toy car, vintage car). (2) About 25 objects have names on the wrong rarity, mostly clean swaps (taxi, van, limousine, drain cover, street lamp, toy car, road sign, hot rod, dolly, pallet jack) or three-way rotations (plough, chairlift, boat trailer, frisbee, sign board, F1). (3) Repeated premises: within objects (smart car parking R/E/L, spinning top R=L, stock car crashing x4, dump trailer E=L, road sign C=E, parking meter R=E, tractor trailer R=L, electric car C=R, coupe C=U) and across objects (pram vs baby carriage E and L; classic car vs vintage car E; classic car L/hearse L vs w05 grille L; combine harvester vs w05 harvester C and L; snow plough U = salt spreader U; tanker L = w05 car L; muscle car L = tow truck L; limousine L = w05 horse cart/bus L; station wagon R/L = w05 car R / rv L; truck E = w01 airedale E). Many Epics are 'carried/cleared every X in town' with no joke. Hard flags: brand/character echoes (snowmobile 'Skidoozer' = Ski-Doo, toy truck 'Big Bob', baby carriage 'Coachella'), 'Gaslight Lane' (meme sense), 'Old Tipsy', 'Choke Out' on a buff, a street sweeper that sucks up children, a runaway pram and a 'Kerb Drop' Ultimate on baby transport, baby powder on a poison move, heat words on poison kits, and effect-specific names on varying Ultimates (Tunnel Whistle, Dizzy Whirl, Bright Night Glare, Underground Steam). Every high and medium item has a concrete replacement; names were checked for length and uniqueness against all curated content and the Pilot 01 proposal.

patterns.pattern: Templated Legendaries: 'has done X for N years / generations', ending on 'still has its original...' or 'never once...'; no outrageous act or punchline.
patterns.suggestion: Keep at most a handful batch-wide; write one concrete outrageous act with a punchline. Replacements for the weakest are in the issues list.

patterns.pattern: Monster names describe another rarity's lore (clean swaps or three-way rotations).
patterns.suggestion: Write names after the lore, line by line. Exact re-pairings are given per object.

patterns.pattern: One premise carried over several rarities of the same object.
patterns.suggestion: Let a trait own at most two rarities; per-object rewrites are in the issues list.

Pairs: pram E/L ~ baby carriage E/L; classic car E = vintage car E; classic car L, hearse L ~ w05 grille L and steamroller L (polished for decades); combine harvester C/L ~ w05 harvester C/L and tractor C; snow plough U = salt spreader U (chips); tanker L = w05 car L (million miles + original trinket); muscle car L = tow truck L (parking space kept for it); limousine L ~ w05 horse cart L + bus L; station wagon R = w05 car R, station wagon L = w05 rv L; truck E ~ w01 airedale E (every parcel, postman); hay baler E ~ w05 hay U (cotton reels), hay baler R ~ w05 harvester R; plough U ~ w05 fishing boat C (gull cloud); cultivator E = seed drill E; stock car C = w05 go-kart C; bollard C = w05 pole C; gondola lift C = w05 cherry picker/scissor lift C; chairlift E ~ train E ('full by nine/ten'); tram and steam locomotive share the epithet 'Queen of the Rails'; taxi L ~ w05 tuk tuk/rickshaw L; hot rod E = w05 airplane E (car alarms); semi trailer C = tanker R (roundabout); tractor R ~ w05 quad tractor L.

patterns.pattern: Epics that carry/clear/serve 'every X in town/county/valley' or 'with a hundred others' with no disruption and no joke.
patterns.suggestion: An Epic needs chaos with a concrete funny consequence; concrete replacements in the issues list.

patterns.pattern: 'Still has its original/same X' Legendary endings.
patterns.suggestion: Retire the 'original trinket' punchline batch-wide; it appears more than 15 times across w05-w06.

patterns.pattern: Legendary name formulas: 56 of 79 start with Grand/Old/Lady/Sir/Captain/Big/Little/Great, 'Grand X-a/-ina of the Y' especially; stems repeat (Puff-, Rosie, Reggie, Rusty, '-alot', '-sworth/-worth').
patterns.suggestion: Vary shapes and avoid reusing personal names across objects.

patterns.pattern: Brands, memes and loaded words in names and moves.
patterns.suggestion: Skidoozer (Ski-Doo), Big Bob (Bob the Builder), Coachella (festival brand), Gaslight Lane (meme), Old Tipsy (drunk), Choke Out (strangle), Tankard (beer mug, low), Weedwhacker (trade name, low), Pony Club (organisation, low). Object labels Formula one, Frisbee and Smart car are brands in the inventory; the writing correctly avoids repeating them.

patterns.pattern: Child-safety tone on baby transport and street machines.
patterns.suggestion: Street sweeper sucking up children, runaway pram Ultimate, 'Kerb Drop' on a pram, racing prams at the sales. Keep babies and children out of harm, even comic harm.

patterns.pattern: Move names that contradict mechanics: heat words on poison kits, fresh smells on poison, sound words on poison, status-specific words on varying Ultimates.
patterns.suggestion: 'Hot Battery/Motor Whiff' -> no heat word; 'Baby Powder Puff' -> a real stink; 'Vroom Noises' -> a smell; Tunnel Whistle / Dizzy / Glare / Steam on varying Ultimates -> effect-neutral.
Give each car its defining feature (minicar roundness, roadster bonnet, coupe doors, hatchback boot, limo length) and let only one of them own parking.
